# Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend — facts

> Source-anchored units about Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend: 19 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 19 units · 6 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] For daily, weekly, and monthly limits, new queries are blocked after exhaustion; running queries can finish when termination is disabled. The periods reset at 00:00 UTC on the next day, Monday, or first of the month, respectively. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] Daily billed-amount threshold alerts exist at organization and project scope, use USD, and ignore credits applied for the previous day. Monthly organization-total and any-project-total threshold alerts are organization-only and reset when the pending invoice closes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] MongoDB recommends billing alerts alongside archive query limits. The alert conditions describe notifications after billing thresholds are exceeded; interpreting an alert as a mechanism that stops archive queries is unsupported by these documents. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/online-archive.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use explain to estimate archive scan volume before regular querying, then scale by expected query frequency. PointFive independently recommends pairing explain with query limits to control per-TB charges. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/online-archive.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend · also: https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/cold-data-kept-on-mongodb-atlas-cluster-storage-instead-of-online-archive

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The archived-data processing rate is $5 per TB with a 10 MB minimum processed per query. This rate does not represent the whole archive bill. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/online-archive.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] OneUptime's March 31, 2026 example derives 82% savings from hot-storage and archive-storage line items alone. Because MongoDB separately bills archive queries and transfers, that example does not establish total savings for a workload that queries its archive. (medium confidence) — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-how-to-use-atlas-online-archive-to-reduce-storage-costs/view · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/online-archive.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Limits can be configured per query, day, week, or month at both project and federated-instance scope; for the same limit type, the more restrictive applicable value wins. Documented allowed values range from 1 GiB to 1 EiB. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] Data Federation supports per-query, daily, weekly, and monthly processing limits at instance and project scope; the more restrictive same-type limit applies. Calendar resets use UTC, with weeks beginning Monday. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] Period limits normally block new queries while running queries finish. Per-query limits attempt termination automatically; optional period-limit termination can overshoot marginally, return ResourceExhausted (402) without results, and still bill processed data. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] PointFive's cost-remediation guidance pairs query limits and explain() for archive reads with revisiting configured cluster storage and tier after archiving. This is its optimization recommendation, not independent measurement of MongoDB's limit enforcement. (low confidence) — https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/cold-data-kept-on-mongodb-atlas-cluster-storage-instead-of-online-archive · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A September 11, 2026 customer feature request reports that Data Federation quota exhaustion prevented production queries for several hours. An October 1 MongoDB response acknowledges the incident and says UI/API quota information does not supply the requested continuous-monitoring metric; the request is Future Consideration, with review timing rather than a delivery commitment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01) — https://feedback.mongodb.com/ideas/CUSTOMER-I-10680 · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] An archive-pricing discussion records a prospective user struggling to estimate spend for approximately 100 GB/day of compliance logs. A respondent warns that archive query and bulk-export costs can be substantial; these are user concerns rather than measured billing benchmarks. (low confidence) — https://www.reddit.com/r/mongodb/comments/1j8uu6o · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Online Archive query limits control data-processing charges, not an all-in archive budget: storage, retrieval, and transfer remain outside that control. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/online-archive.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md
- [statement] Data Federation query limits apply to processed data only; they do not cap retrieval or transfer charges. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] The documented default for new federated instances is 100 TB processed monthly. Project limits are enforced per cloud object storage; the documentation's AWS-plus-Azure example permits 200 TB total across two 100 TB instances. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] Per-query limits attempt termination by default. Optional termination for period limits can exceed the threshold marginally, returns no results and ResourceExhausted code 402, and still bills for data processed before termination. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/manage-query-limits.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] Atlas recommends billing alerts and billing-page cost visualizations or invoices for archive spend. The federated-instance page shows processed/returned data and query counts but does not show archive cost. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/online-archive.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
- [statement] As a design recommendation, keep routine recent-data reads on the cluster and reserve the federated endpoint for historical queries; frequent broad archive analytics can accumulate query charges. TideWave presents separate live/history clients, while PointFive recommends query limits for archive reads. (high confidence) — https://tidewave.net/blog/atlas-online-archive-tiering-cold-data-to-cut-costs · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend · also: https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/cold-data-kept-on-mongodb-atlas-cluster-storage-instead-of-online-archive
- [statement] MongoDB recommends estimating monthly processing from explain results multiplied by expected query count. The archive's federated-instance page shows processing, returned data, and query counts; actual archive costs appear on the Atlas billing page. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/online-archive.md · keywords: Query limits and billing alerts for archive spend
